record.paper_title: Semigroups of rational functions: some problems and conjectures
record.original_question: Let A and B be rational functions of degree at least two. If some forward orbit of A has infinite intersection with some forward orbit of B, must A and B have a common iterate?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.4. Let A and B be rational functions of degree at least two such that an orbit of A has an infinite intersection with an orbit of B. Then A and B have a common iterate.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ and $B$ be rational functions of degree at least two, viewed as self-maps of the Riemann sphere $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$. For a rational function $f$ and a point $z_0 \in \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$, the forward orbit of $z_0$ under $f$ is the set $\mathcal{O}_f(z_0) = \{z_0, f(z_0), f^{\circ 2}(z_0), f^{\circ 3}(z_0), \dots\}$, where $f^{\circ n}$ denotes the $n$-fold compositional iterate of $f$. Two rational functions $A$ and $B$ are said to have a common iterate if there exist positive integers $m, n$ such that $A^{\circ m} = B^{\circ n}$.

Prove or disprove: if there exist points $a, b \in \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ such that the intersection $\mathcal{O}_A(a) \cap \mathcal{O}_B(b)$ is infinite, then $A$ and $B$ must have a common iterate.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture has been established in significant special cases — for nonlinear complex polynomials of equal degree (Ghioca–Tucker–Zieve, Inventiones 2008) and more generally for tame rational functions (Pakovich, JEMS), where infinite orbit intersection is shown to imply a common iterate. The full conjecture for arbitrary rational functions of degree at least two over $\mathbb{C}$ does not appear to have been resolved; in positive characteristic counterexamples exist. Thus the problem is partially solved but remains open in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Tame rational functions: Decompositions of iterates and orbit intersections
status_evidence.snippet: For tame rational functions A and B, if orbits have infinite intersection, then A and B have a common iterate.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is proven for the class of tame rational functions.

status_evidence.title: Intersections of polynomial orbits, and a dynamical Mordell–Lang conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Nonlinear complex polynomials of the same degree have a common iterate if their orbits have infinite intersection.
status_evidence.claim: Established for nonlinear complex polynomials of the same degree.

status_evidence.title: Intersection of orbits for polynomials in characteristic p
status_evidence.snippet: Counterexamples in positive characteristic to the strong common-iterate conclusion.
status_evidence.claim: The analogous statement fails in positive characteristic, indicating the problem is delicate.
